clue.text: Throw beginner in behind jetty

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, as a bowler or pitcher does

indicators.note: the beginner's letter is set in the middle of the word for behind

parts.note: the back is the part behind
L is the learner plate, a beginner's sign

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a novice into the water off the back of a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jetty' looks like a pier, but here it is the adjective from jet, the glossy black stone. 'in' puts L inside BACK to make BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is a deep black mineral, so jetty means intensely black, as dark as pitch.

clue.text: Ways in which father gets this, but not I

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the clue tells us to take the word this without the letter I

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent is given something, though the speaker is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths are routes or tracks, the ways by which one travels.

clue.text: Procrastinate when it's time to get up

parts.note: tempo is musical time, the speed of a piece
to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: Dithering in the morning when the alarm says it's time to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay a decision in order to gain time, a form of stalling.

clue.text: Dive after the ball, flat out

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable den, and a hell is an old word for a gambling den
for can mean in pursuit of, as in going for something
a cricket ball is called the leather, from its covering

explanation.surface: A fielder hurls himself full length to stop the ball, ending up sprawled flat on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the ball is often called 'the leather'. 'Dive' and 'flat out' suggest a sporting dive, but 'flat out' means at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at full tilt, as fast as possible, is the idiom of riding at breakneck speed.

clue.text: Prisoner has to pull up — he's fallen behind

parts.note: an old lag is a long-serving convict

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for pull is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag is to pull along

explanation.surface: A convict hauled back into line after straggling behind the group.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict. 'up' turns DRAG into GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a straggler, someone slow who trails the rest.

clue.text: What's inside, please?

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks to know what a parcel holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Content is the matter held inside something, and as a verb it means to satisfy or gratify someone.

clue.text: Some reckless pedestrians went too fast

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few careless walkers rushed along the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, to move faster than allowed.

clue.text: Ezra's money

explanation.surface: A poet's cash, as if asking what Ezra earned.
explanation.definitionFit: The American poet Ezra Pound bore this surname, and the British unit of currency shares the name.

clue.text: Gave evidence about it that's set down

indicators.note: the word for gave evidence is wrapped about the word it

parts.note: to depose is to testify under oath, so gave evidence is deposed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness testified about something that had been recorded in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' a subject, but it is the container signal; 'Gave evidence' is the legal sense of depose, to testify under oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deposited has been laid or placed down somewhere.

clue.text: Making an impression upon land resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first word sits upon the second

parts.note: stamping is pressing a mark or impression into something
ground is land or earth

explanation.surface: Leaving footprints on the earth at a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamping ground is a favourite haunt, a place one habitually frequents.

clue.text: Girl, put out, comes back in the meantime

indicators.note: the joined words for girl and put out are read from right to left

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to emit is to give out or discharge

explanation.surface: A young woman, upset at being sent away, returns in the interim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' reverses the whole of GALEMIT. 'put out' looks like 'annoyed' but means EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is the interval between two events, the time in between.

clue.text: Chicane describes this bridge hand

parts.note: in bridge, a chicane is a hand holding not a single card of the trump suit

explanation.surface: A card term is defined, though chicane suggests a twisty bit of racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: A chicane is also a bend on a motor-racing circuit, but in bridge it names a hand void of trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand with no trumps lacks the trump suit entirely, which is exactly what a chicane is.

clue.text: Wolf chewed up and swallowed by reptile in some precipitation

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the word for reptile

parts.note: a snake is a legless reptile

indicators.note: the word wolf is mangled into a new order, as if chewed

explanation.surface: A predator is mauled and eaten by a serpent during a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed up' is the anagram signal, and 'swallowed by' says the scrambled predator ends up inside the serpent, just as the surface pictures it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake of snow is a single crystal of falling weather, one bit of precipitation.

clue.text: On reflection, I am sorry about king

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the short form of I am is read backwards

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for sorry is read backwards

parts.note: sad is sorry or regretful

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, someone apologises regarding a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns IM into MI and 'about' turns SAD into DAS. Midas is the legendary king whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas was the mythical Phrygian monarch granted the golden touch.

clue.text: About one, brother rose

indicators.note: the word for brother goes about the letter for one

parts.note: Brer is a dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Regarding one person, a brother stood up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb but is the flower; 'About' puts BRER around I.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet brier is a wild rose, so the name stands for that flowering shrub.

clue.text: Little woman should get remembered

parts.note: Beth March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
ought means should

explanation.surface: A small lady ought to be recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' looks like a small lady, but it points to Beth, one of the March sisters in Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: To bethink oneself is an old phrase for to recall, so bethought means recalled.

clue.text: Disastrously terminated — not a disadvantage

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of terminated are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something ended in catastrophe, though apparently that did no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes one A from TERMINATED; 'Disastrously' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or damage, something that puts one at a loss.

clue.text: Leader in rioting, I led a riot

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ringleader in a disturbance confesses to having started it.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a newspaper's main opinion piece; the riot is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the editor's opinion column, the main article stating the paper's view.

clue.text: So in that respect, take care!

parts.note: there can mean on that point, as in there I agree
fore is the golfer's shouted warning to watch out for the ball

explanation.surface: A warning to be careful about that particular matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take care!' is FORE, the golfer's warning cry.
explanation.definitionFit: So and therefore both mean as a consequence, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Late deliveries expected

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls delivered by a bowler
due means expected or anticipated

explanation.surface: Parcels arriving behind schedule had been awaited.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six balls bowled in cricket, so 'deliveries' is a cricket term here, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past the expected time, behind schedule.

clue.text: Local case finally has CID men going haywire

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word case
something going haywire runs out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood crime ends up with detectives in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police Criminal Investigation Department. 'finally' gives E, the last letter of case; 'going haywire' turns CID MEN into NDEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic means native to or confined to a particular place or people.

clue.text: Pound note outside

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
rind is the outer skin of fruit or cheese

explanation.surface: A banknote's exterior, as if describing a sterling note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like currency but is the verb, to crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind is to crush to powder, which is what pounding in a mortar does.

clue.text: Caught away from shelter, out in the open

indicators.note: the letter for caught is taken away from the word for shelter

parts.note: a covert is a thicket giving shelter to game
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone trapped away from cover is exposed in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: A covert is a thicket where game hides; C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden or secret.

clue.text: Gladden the heart of kindred

indicators.note: the heart is what remains when the first and last letters of the word for kindred are removed

parts.note: related means of the same family, kindred

explanation.surface: Cheer up the very core of one's family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' strips R and D from RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to fill them with joy, to cheer them up.

clue.text: Cover rearranged — owner died

indicators.note: the letters of owner died are put into a different order

explanation.surface: After the proprietor's death, a bedspread is changed around.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with duck feathers, a bed covering.

clue.text: Black king captured in one move

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
the letters of the word one are moved into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A dark chess king is taken in a single turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges the word one into NEO, with 'captured in' as the container signal. The chess surface hides Georgius Rex, the royal cipher seen on British post boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish and Italian the word means the colour black; in English it is a dated, now offensive, term for a Black person.

clue.text: Enterprising leader of Indian territory

parts.note: Goa is a former Portuguese territory, now a state of India
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: Describing an ambitious ruler of a region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person is ambitious and keen on progress, eager to push forward.

clue.text: Beating back love in Pacific island

indicators.note: the whole combination is then read backwards
the word for love goes inside the island

parts.note: Guam is an island in the western Pacific
love means nil or zero in tennis scores

explanation.surface: A thrashing returns affection on a South Sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'back' reverses everything, so the island comes out as MAUG. Love means zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A mauling is a severe battering or thrashing.

clue.text: He joins a bank

explanation.surface: Describing a man who takes up a job at a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ties things together joins them; a bank of seats or rows is a series of ranks, one above another.

clue.text: Minor crime — one cop called out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A petty offence: a police officer was summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I with COP and CALLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or trivial misdeed.
